correctness.rationale: Exact Pythagorean mate and canonical norm give the reflected Toeplitz Gram. Bidiagonal elimination proves determinant and positive tridiagonal inverse. The alternating inverse Rayleigh vector controls the smallest eigenvalue uniformly. Uniform convergence of appropriately normalized step kernels plus Sturm–Liouville analysis yields every fixed-index eigenvalue in the finite crossover. A norm upper bound and last-block constant vector match in the separated regime. The 405 finite checker assertions corroborate identities but do not prove infinite limits.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected primary manuscript supplies the canonical monomial norm and boundary linear symbol, but not the joint finite-degree/near-extreme fixed-index spectral limit, sharp Dirichlet–Robin law, or uniform optimal condition-number crossover. Ordinary Kac–Murdock–Szegő covariance results have a distinct stationary Toeplitz matrix, while the new Gram matrix contains a hard-boundary reflected term. The general Green-kernel methods and the exact factorization are classical; novelty is claimed narrowly for the combined de Branges–Rovnyak near-extreme asymptotic. Equivalence in older AR covariance literature remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Local-to-unity autoregressive covariance theorems may yield the same Robin Green spectrum by a straightforward reflected-matrix specialization; global priority is not certified.

value.rationale: Near-extreme polynomial Gram conditioning is a natural quantitative invariant governing stable degree truncations in a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space. The theorem determines the critical parameter scale, all fixed-index spectral constants and the exact separated asymptotic, rather than a routine endpoint norm or a renaming of stationary Toeplitz eigenvalues. The reflected half-line boundary is essential to the Robin limit.
